proofs.locator: PDF pp.18–19 Lemmas 1–2, Eq.(51)–(53); p.22 §4.2; pp.23–24 Lemma 5, Eq.(61), and Proof of Theorem 2(a), Eq.(62)
map: Source dependencies, pp.18–19: Lemma 1 uses prox optimality and the Bregman three-point identity to bound the prox objective by the comparator objective minus V at the new center. Lemma 2 gives 0≤Ψ(y)−Ψ(x)−〈g(x),y−x〉≤(L/2)||y−x||²+2M||y−x|| under the paper's subgradient convention. Eq.(53) bounds bu−au²/2 by b²/(2a). These are internal source dependencies, not separate unreviewed library records.

p.22 defines δ_t=G(x_t^md,ξ_t)−g(x_t^md). Lemma 5, pp.23–24, uses x_{t+1}^ag−x_t^md=β_t^{-1}(x_{t+1}−x_t), Lemma 2, strong convexity of the generator, convexity of Ψ, Eq.(53), and Lemma 1 applied to the linear stochastic prox objective. It obtains β_tγ_t[Ψ(x_{t+1}^ag)−Ψ(x)]+V(x_{t+1},x)≤(β_t−1)γ_t[Ψ(x_t^ag)−Ψ(x)]+V(x_t,x)+Δ_t(x), with Δ_t(x)=γ_t〈δ_t,x−x_t〉+(2M+||δ_t||_*)²β_tγ_t²/[2(αβ_t−Lγ_t)].

p.24: choose a fixed minimizer x*. Nonnegative objective gaps and (β_{t+1}−1)γ_{t+1}≤β_tγ_t allow telescoping. β1=1 removes the initial gap and Eq.(15) bounds V(x1,x*)≤D²; the final divergence is nonnegative.
p.24: the iterate triple is measurable with respect to ξ[ t−1 ]. Under A1, E[ζ_t|ξ[ t−1 ]]=0 and E||δ_t||_*²≤σ². Taking expectation in Eq.(62) and dividing by its positive prefactor proves part (a).

assumptions: f:X→R is convex and satisfies ||∇f(x)−∇f(y)||_*≤L||x−y|| for all x,y∈X. h:X→R is convex with |h(x)−h(y)|≤M||x−y|| for all x,y∈X.
For all x,x′∈X°, 〈∇ω(x′)−∇ω(x),x′−x〉≥α||x′−x||². The prox subproblems are solved exactly, with minimizers in X°.

A1: for each x∈X, the Borel Oracle map satisfies E G(x,ξ)=g(x)∈∂Ψ(x) and E||G(x,ξ)−g(x)||_*²≤σ². At each iteration ξ_t is a fresh draw independent of the previous draw history and hence of the current query point.
The deterministic sequences satisfy β1=1, β_t≥1, γ_t>0, and for every integer t≥1: 0<(β_{t+1}−1)γ_{t+1}≤β_tγ_t and 2Lγ_t≤αβ_t.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let X⊂R^n be nonempty compact convex, with inner product, norm ||·|| and dual ||·||_*. Set Ψ=f+h and Ψ*=min_{x∈X}Ψ(x). Let ω:X→R be continuous convex. Define X°={x∈X: x∈argmin_{u∈X}[〈p,u〉+ω(u)] for some p∈R^n}; require X° convex and ω continuously differentiable there. Set V(x,z)=ω(z)−ω(x)−〈∇ω(x),z−x〉, P_x(y)=argmin_{z∈X}{〈y,z−x〉+V(x,z)}, and D²=max_Xω−min_Xω. Subgradients at relative-interior points lie in lin(X−X); boundary subgradients are limits of these along convergent sequences, as in §1.1. Initialize x1∈argmin_Xω and x1^ag=x1. Define x_t^md=β_t^{-1}x_t+(1−β_t^{-1})x_t^ag, x_{t+1}=P_{x_t}(γ_tG(x_t^md,ξ_t)), and x_{t+1}^ag=β_t^{-1}x_{t+1}+(1−β_t^{-1})x_t^ag.
statement.parameter_domains: Finite dimensions n,d; α>0; finite L,M,σ≥0; β_t∈[1,∞), γ_t>0. No Euclidean-ball restriction, strong convexity of Ψ or positive lower bound on L,M,σ is imposed. The denominator is strictly positive by Eq.(30).
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every instance satisfying the assumptions, every such deterministic step sequence, and every integer N≥1, the conclusion holds with expectation over ξ1,…,ξN, which are iid with common law P on Ξ⊆R^d. The output is the prescribed AC-SA aggregate. Freshness is conditional on the past; future adaptive query points need not be independent of earlier draws.

summary: For AC-SA under A1 and the coupled step conditions (30), the aggregate expected gap is bounded by the initial distance-generator range plus a squared-step noise/nonsmoothness term, divided by (β_{N+1}−1)γ_{N+1}.
title: AC-SA expected-gap bound for admissible step sequences
use_when: Bound AC-SA aggregate expected error for a supplied admissible deterministic step schedule.
